findings.title: Some escaped headers are no longer valid JSON strings
findings.description: For code points above U+FFFF, `oneLine()` now writes `\u{XXXXX}`, and `\u{` is not a valid JSON escape. `check` wraps the header in `JSON.stringify` and then passes it through `oneLine`, so a header with a supplementary-plane format character (for example the tag characters U+E0001–U+E007F or U+1D173–U+1D17A) prints a `fail` line whose quoted header fails `JSON.parse`, even though criterion 4 says the header is written as a JSON string. The config error lines (lines 105 and 111) quote the path the same way, so they break in the same way.

findings.title: Header doc says unchanged but the text is normalized
findings.description: The doc comment on `CheckedCommit.header` says it is the "First line of the commit message, unchanged", but `checkGitLog` takes it from `ParsedCommit.raw`, which `normalize()` has already stripped of CRs and trailing whitespace. A library caller who reads the exported type will expect git's exact bytes, which also contradicts the revised criterion 4 in the ticket.

findings.title: Check output drops skipped merge commits
findings.description: The `check` branch in `src/cli.ts` builds stdout from failing commits, malformed records, and the summary without printing `skip <short sha> merge commit` for skipped merges. When the input contains merge commits, maintainers and CI see only the skipped count, and the all-merge test still passes because it checks only the exit code and summary.

review_agent_comment: Before this leaves draft, please consider tracking the accepted header-whitespace/BOM behavior in a follow-up ticket, and decide whether `check` should fail when it checks zero commits. Longer term, consider escaping echoed arguments consistently across commands so diagnostics cannot contain forged lines. When this PR claims T-009, update its BACKLOG status to `done (PR n)` for the ticket-link check.
